subject: Quickstart CTA: developer demo availability and technical intake
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@skyline.dev>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quickstart CTA: looking to book technical demo for developer team

Hi Chloe,

I hit the Quickstart CTA after testing Redwood with our prototype and would like to schedule a technical demo to walk my engineering team through integration patterns (model routing, caching, and private deployment options). We're a small infra team at Skyline (3 engineers + 1 product manager). Developer intent: we want to move from prototype -> PoC in the next 4–6 weeks.

Preferred window: mornings PST (9–12) next week. If you need a quick summary of our use case: our product enriches logs with embeddings for search and chat; latency matters (<=150ms p50) and we have some PII considerations.

Can you point me to an available SE and some slots? Happy to share a short doc with current architecture.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Director of Engineering, Skyline
samir@skyline.dev
+1 (415) 555-0198
From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@skyline.dev>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quickstart CTA: looking to book technical demo for developer team

Hi Samir — thanks for reaching out and for trying the Quickstart guide.

Looping in Ben (SE) for the technical deep-dive and Ava (our SDR) to coordinate timing. Ben, Samir's team is focused on embeddings + low-latency search with PII constraints — wants a PoC in 4–6 weeks.

Ben, would one of these windows work for a 45–60 minute session (we can tailor the agenda to KV cache, routing fallbacks, and deployment options)?
- Tue 8/24: 9:30–10:30am PST
- Wed 8/25: 10:00–11:00am PST

If neither works, please propose two alternate slots. Samir — if you'd rather pick from our booking page, here's a short availability link: https://calendar.redwood.com/s/ava-chen/quickstart (we'll send a formal invite once you confirm). Also adding a HubSpot record for this contact: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890

Next steps: pick a slot or reply with preferred times and timezone. I'll leave the technical agenda to Ben.

—Chloe
Chloe Martin
Enterprise SDR Lead, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>, Samir Gupta <samir@skyline.dev>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 11:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quickstart CTA: looking to book technical demo for developer team

Thanks Chloe — happy to run the session. Samir, quick questions to make the demo high-signal:
1) Which runtime are you prototyping on (managed cloud, self-hosted GPU, or hybrid)?
2) Do you have sample sequences or expected prompt lengths (avg/peak) so I can show batching/quantization tradeoffs?
3) Any specific compliance concerns (e.g., retention/Audit logs or KMS integration)?

I can do the slots Chloe proposed, plus: Thu 8/26 9:00–10:00am PST. For the meeting I'll bring:
- short agenda (intro, architecture review, demo: routing & KV caching, Q&A)
- pre-demo checklist (attached) — please fill in the infra bits if convenient

If you confirm a time I'll send a calendar invite with a short mutual action plan attached.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachments: pre-demo-checklist.docx (see list of infra items to surface ahead of time)

Hi Chloe and Ben — thanks for the quick follow-up and the checklist. We're actually on East Coast time (my mistake earlier) so mornings EST are easier for us. From the proposed options, could we move to one of these EDT slots instead?
- Tue 8/24: 12:30–1:30pm EDT (corresponds to 9:30am PST)
- Wed 8/25: 1:00–2:00pm EDT (corresponds to 10:00am PST)

Either works for the team; prefer Tue if Ben is available. I'll fill the checklist and attach a short architecture diagram before the meeting. Please send a calendar invite and I'll accept.

Also, can you include a brief section on routing fallbacks — specifically around preferring cheaper variants automatically when load spikes — that's a key decision point for us.

Thanks,
